title: Relaxing Your Entire Body
summary: Rest from head to feet and learn palm and sole.
script:
Let your eyes close, gently, like a curtain closing at the end of a quiet day. Or, if you prefer, let them rest softly, looking down, unfocused.

For these next few minutes, there's nothing you need to do, and nothing you need to think about. Just this. Just you, resting here.

Feel the surface beneath you, supporting you completely. Notice your body sinking a little, becoming heavier, more still.

Take a slow breath in… and let it out.

One more. In… and out.

Today, we're going to bring our attention to two parts of the body that carry us through every single day, often without much thanks. Your hands, and your feet.

We rarely stop to notice them. They work quietly, constantly, holding things, carrying us, touching the world around us. Today, we'll give them the attention they deserve.

Let's begin with your hands. Bring your awareness there now. Notice how they feel, resting, doing nothing at all.

In the center of each hand, there is a part called the palm. Your palm is the soft, inside surface of your hand, the inside part of your hand where your fingers begin.

Bring your attention to your palms now. Notice if they feel warm, or cool. Notice if they feel open, or slightly closed.

Imagine, for a moment, that your palms are resting in warm sunlight. Feel this warmth spreading slowly across them, soft and comforting.

Let your palms soften completely. Let them feel open, relaxed, asking for nothing, holding nothing.

Notice your fingers too, resting beside your palms. Let them curl, ever so slightly, the way they naturally want to do.

Your hands have touched so many things. Held so many things. And right now, they can simply rest, empty, and calm.

Take a slow breath in, and imagine that breath moving all the way down into your palms. Breathe out, and feel your palms grow even softer, even heavier.

Now, let's move our attention down to your feet.

At the bottom of each foot, there is a part called the sole. Your sole is the underside of your foot, the part that touches the ground every time you walk, every time you stand.

Bring your awareness there now. Notice your soles, resting against the surface beneath you, or resting gently in the air if your feet are raised.

Think about everything your feet carry you through, every single day. Every step, every place you've walked, every doorway you've crossed. Your soles have felt the ground beneath countless moments of your life, and they rarely receive a single thought of gratitude.

Let's give them that thought now.

Imagine warm sand beneath your soles, soft and fine, still warm from the afternoon sun. Feel the gentle weight of it, pressing softly against your skin.

Let your soles soften completely. Let any tightness there melt slowly away, sinking into that warm, soft sand.

Take a slow breath in, sending your awareness down into your feet. Breathe out, and let your soles feel completely at rest, heavy, and calm.

Notice now, both your palms and your soles, resting quietly. Your palms, facing gently upward or resting softly at your sides. Your soles, resting against the ground, or floating gently in stillness.

These two parts of your body rarely touch each other, rarely share the same kind of attention. But right now, in this moment, they are both completely relaxed, both completely still.

Let this stillness spread. From your palms, up through your arms, into your shoulders. From your soles, up through your legs, into your hips.

Meeting somewhere in the middle, in your chest, where your breath continues, slow and steady, in and out.

Notice how connected your whole body feels right now. Every part playing its role. Every part, right now, simply resting.

There's something quietly beautiful about hands and feet. They ask for so little, and yet they carry us through everything. Every hug we give, every step we take, begins with them.

Today, let this be a small thank you. A few quiet minutes of rest, for parts of you that rarely stop working.

Let these gentle words settle into your mind.

My palms are open, and calm.

My soles are soft, and supported.

My body carries me gently, through each day.

I am grateful for this body.

I am completely at rest.

Take another slow breath, and let these words settle deeper.

Stay here a little longer, noticing this quiet connection between your hands and your feet. Both resting. Both still. Both completely at peace.

There's no need to rush away from this feeling. Let it stay with you for as long as you'd like, this sense of your whole body, cared for, and calm.

When you feel ready, and only when you feel ready, begin to bring a little movement back. Not quickly, just a small awakening.

Notice your palms first. Let your fingers stretch out, slowly, like they're waking up after a long, peaceful rest.

Then notice your soles. Let your toes move gently, just slightly, feeling the surface beneath them once again.

Take a breath in, and let it fill your whole body. Breathe out, slow and complete.

Whenever you're ready, let your eyes open softly, taking in the light around you.

Before you continue with your day, take one more moment. Look at your hands, if you can. Notice your palms. Think about everything they've done for you, and everything they'll continue to do.

And remember, even when you're standing, even when you're walking through your busiest moments, your soles are still there, quietly supporting you, one step at a time.

Carry this small awareness with you. A little gratitude, for two parts of you that ask for very little, and give so much.

You are calm. You are supported. And you are exactly where you need to be.

vocabulary.definition: the soft inside surface of your hand, where your fingers begin
the underside of your foot, the part that touches the ground when you walk or stand
